title: JUSINOVA v. NORTH MACEDONIA
full_text: FIFTH SECTION DECISION Application no. 59492/18 Mizafer JUSINOVA against North Macedonia (see appended table) The European Court of Human Rights (Fifth Section), sitting on 21 January 2021 as a Committee composed of: Ganna Yudkivska, President, Ivana Jelić, Arnfinn Bårdsen, judges, and Liv Tigerstedt, Acting Deputy Section Registrar, Having regard to the above application lodged on 7 December 2018, Having regard to the formal declarations accepting a friendly settlement of the case, Having deliberated, decides as follows: FACTS AND PROCEDURE The applicant’s details are set out in the appended table. The applicant was represented by European Roma Rights Centre, a non ‑ governmental organisation based in Brussels. The applicant’s complaints under Article 2 of the Convention concerning the death of her brother, a young man of Roma origin who died while serving a prison sentence, were communicated to the Government of the Republic of North Macedonia (“the Government”). The Court received the friendly-settlement declaration, signed by the parties, under which the applicant agreed to waive any further claims against North Macedonia in respect of the facts giving rise to this application, subject to an undertaking by the Government to pay her the amount detailed in the appended table. This amount will be converted into the currency of the respondent State at the rate applicable on the date of payment, and will be payable within three months from the date of notification of the Court’s decision. In the event of failure to pay this amount within the above-mentioned three-month period, the Government undertake to pay simple interest on it, from the expiry of that period until settlement, at a rate equal to the marginal lending rate of the European Central Bank during the default period plus three percentage points. The payment will constitute the final resolution of the case. THE LAW The Court takes note of the friendly settlement reached between the parties. It is satisfied that the settlement is based on respect for human rights as defined in the Convention and the Protocols thereto and finds no reasons to justify a continued examination of the application. In view of the above, it is appropriate to strike the case out of the list. For these reasons, the Court, unanimously, Decides to strike the application out of its list of cases in accordance with Article 39 of the Convention. Done in English and notified in writing on 11 February 2021. ure_p_1} {signature_p_2} Liv Tigerstedt Ganna Yudkivska Acting Deputy Registrar President APPENDIX Application raising complaints under Article 2 of the Convention Application no. summary: Mizafer Jusinova, a member of the Roma community, brought a case against North Macedonia to the European Court of Human Rights. The case centered on the vulnerability of Roma individuals in detention, specifically concerning the death of Jusinova's brother, a young Roma man, while serving a prison sentence. The applicant, represented by the European Roma Rights Centre, alleged a violation of Article 2 of the European Convention on Human Rights, which protects the right to life. The Court communicated the complaint to the North Macedonian government. However, the case was resolved through a friendly settlement, with the government agreeing to compensate Jusinova with €12,000 for pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages. Consequently, the Court struck the case out of its list under Article 39, as the settlement respected human rights principles. This case highlights the ongoing issues faced by Roma individuals in detention, reflecting broader historical patterns of discrimination and marginalization of Roma communities in Europe. The resolution through a friendly settlement underscores the importance of addressing such vulnerabilities through legal and compensatory measures.
